findings.headline: The source catalog is balanced across four high-pressure application categories.
findings.interpretation: This was a deliberate sampling frame, not an estimate of category prevalence.

findings.headline: Application guidance is split across web pages and downloadable files.
findings.interpretation: Applicants often need to collect instructions from more than one format; the index preserves direct source URLs.

findings.headline: The public guidance ecosystem is fragmented across authorities, institutions, and private operators.
findings.metric: 21 government/public-authority sources; 16 financial/GSE sources; 12 education/public-institution sources
findings.interpretation: No single checklist should be treated as universal. The actual requester’s current instructions control.

findings.headline: Deep-reviewed primary sources repeatedly center factual identity, income/employment, assets/funds, and traceable support.
findings.interpretation: This pattern is a preparation framework, not a claim that every one of the 100 cataloged sources asks for every field.

limitations: The 100-source catalog records public source metadata and URLs. Most records were not coded line-by-line in this release.
Only records marked deepContentCoding=true support item-level preparation-signal findings.
Requirements change by requester, jurisdiction, program, and date.
The report does not measure approval odds, market share, ranking, or applicant outcomes.
